newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sterling strength boosts Elsevier dividend.
newsitem.headline: Sterling strength boosts Elsevier dividend.

text.p: Sterling' recent spurt was the reason for a 29 percent increase in the 1996 dividend of Elsevier NV to 0.76 guilders, deputy chairman Paul Vlek said.

Vlek told a results presentation on Wednesday that the relatively large increase in the Elsevier dividend was caused by Reed Elsevier's policy of converting it from sterling just before the group's results were announced.
The final Elsevier dividend was converted at a rate of 3.10 guilders to the pound.
Elsevier's earnings per share rose 13 percent to 1.13 guilders, but these were converted at the average 1996 exchange rate of 2.63 guilders to the pound, up from 2.53 in 1995.
Reed's gross dividend rose 11 percent to 34.0 pence with earnings per share up nine percent to 56.2 pence.
Elsevier NV chairman Herman Bruggink said he expected sterling to remain strong versus the guilder in 1997.
This was an exception to the rule for Elsevier which has often seen a negative impact on its earnings per share in previous years as a result of the guilder appreciating against the pound, he said.
